findings.description: A regular expression used for email validation is vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS).
findings.reasoning: The regular expression exhibits a pattern known to cause ReDoS. The sub-pattern `(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*` contains nested quantifiers (`*` and `?`) that apply to overlapping patterns. This allows for a very large number of ways for the regex engine to match the input, leading to exponential matching time on certain inputs. An attacker can craft a string that triggers this backtracking, leading to a denial of service.

evidence.notes: The vulnerability exists in the domain matching part of the regex: `(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*`. The combination of nested optional (`?`) and repeated (`*`) groups for a similar pattern (`[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9]`) can lead to catastrophic backtracking when the regex engine processes certain inputs.
